newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. to recognise HK post-handover passports-paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to recognise HK post-handover passports-paper.

text.p: A senior United States official said Washington would recognise the Hong Kong passports to be issued after the British colony reverts to China next year, a pro-Beijing newspaper reported on Saturday.
But the report in Wen Wei Po, which quoted an unidentified U.S. official in Washington, did not specify if the country would grant visa-free access to post-1997 Hong Kong passport holders.
The United States would handle visa applications from Hong Kong residents separately from those of mainland Chinese after the sovereignty transfer, the newspaper quoted him as saying.
The British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 and becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.

After the handover, the new Hong Kong authority will issue SAR passports to eligible citizens. But very few major countries apart from Britain have said so far they will recognise the SAR passport and allow visa-free entry.
The U.S. official also said China and the United States were very likely to agree to keep the U.S. consulate in Hong Kong after the handover, Wen Wei Po reported.
The pact, if clinched, would be announced on November 19 during a visit by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher to China from November 18 to 21, he was quoted as saying.
Officials at the U.S. consulate and China's diplomatic mission in Hong Kong were not available to comment.
